title: Metric Registry & Scorer SDK for Quantized Profile Validation
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Our current quantization validation pipelines wire together a grab-bag of ad-hoc metric implementations (perplexity scripts, MMLU harnesses, BLEU/ROUGE wrappers, and bespoke task scorers). This makes it hard to reuse metrics across calibration runs, compare outputs consistently, or add new referenceless scorers. Scope: Build a lightweight Metric Registry and Scorer SDK that standardizes metric contracts and provides an extensible plugin surface for: 1) token-level and sequence-level metrics (perplexity, cross-entropy), 2) benchmark suites (MMLU-style multiple-choice and ranking), 3) summarization metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/SBERT similarity), and 4) task-specific scorers (QA F1, code-exec correctness). Deliverables: (a) Python SDK with a Metric base class, standardized output envelope, and eval runner CLI; (b) registry service (file-backed + optional runtime discovery) for cataloging metric implementations and versions; (c) adapters for existing eval harnesses and the calibration pipeline; (d) CI checks and a small dashboard-ready JSON schema used by the Console for quality regression alerts. Goals: make metric addition a one-file change and ensure results are comparable across FP8/INT8 calibration runs and baseline FP32 runs.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a Metric abstract class with methods: init(config), score(predictions, references, metadata), and explain()
Metric outputs conform to the platform envelope: {metric_id, version, score_type, value, confidence?, per_example?: []} (serialized as JSON)
Implementations included: Perplexity (streaming-capable), MMLU multiple-choice harness, ROUGE & BLEU wrappers, and a template for task-specific scorers
Registry can load local plugins and list metadata (name, version, supported_input_types) from a manifest
Calibration pipeline can switch metric sets via config and produce identical envelope schema for downstream gating
Unit tests covering edge cases: long sequences (perplexity approx windowing), no-reference tasks, and batched scoring
PR with docs, CLI usage examples, and two sample metric plugins merged to main branch
Console hookup: produced JSON artifacts are parsable by existing regression alerting consumer (schema validated)

Observations: computing true perplexity across very long sequences is expensive; implemented windowed-likelihood approximation as a trade-off. Posted prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval/tree/spike/metric-sdk
